answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can be achieved through localized trust graphs where each agent acts as a vertex in an interconnected web of verifiable interactions. Rather than relying on simple staking, the network evaluates transitive credit flows, ensuring fraudulent identities are isolated before they scale. Even when an ocean of synthetic accounts attempts to manipulate consensus, the incoming tide of coordinated activity is dampened by clustering algorithms that penalize coordinated topology. This keeps artificial consensus from polluting decentralized decisions.
